# Baghdad 830 – Energy & engines

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Animal-powered machines (horse gin, treadwheel)** [`animal_power_gin`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/animal_power_gin.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Ox- and donkey-driven saqiya wheels lift water all over the Sawad; animal mills grind grain in town. Camels and mules carry the empire's freight. Local: saqiya wheels on canal banks; donkey mills of Karkh.
- **Water wheel** [`water_wheel`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_wheel.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Current-driven norias lift water on the Euphrates and Orontes; water mills turn on canals. Floating ship mills on the Tigris are described in the 10th century at Mosul and may already exist. Local: norias on the Euphrates (Anbar, Hit); mills on the Nahr Isa and Sarat canals. Elsewhere: Hama on the Orontes: great norias.
- **Windmill** [`windmill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept high. The first clear evidence of vertical-axis windmills in Sistan is 9th-century, the first descriptions 10th-century (al-Mas'udi); the story of a Persian windmill-builder in 644 is later legend. In 830 they may exist in Sistan, a rumour in Baghdad. Elsewhere: Sistan (eastern Iran), steady summer wind.
- **Water turbine** [`water_turbine`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/water_turbine.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept high. Horizontal mill wheels driven by a jet from a drop tower are common in Iran and Syria. Shaping blades for efficiency and enclosing the wheel is the new part.
- **Crank, connecting rod and flywheel** [`crank_connecting_rod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crank_connecting_rod.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Hand cranks on querns and rotary grindstones exist. Turning rotation into back-and-forth with a connecting rod is not in use; al-Jazari's crank pump is four centuries off.
- **Piston pumps (suction and force pump)** [`piston_pump`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/piston_pump.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept medium. Ctesibius' force pump is in Greek mechanics (Hero, Philo) and the naphtha syringe is used in war. Water is lifted by noria, saqiya and shaduf, so nobody needs a pump yet. Local: naffatun (naphtha troops) with brass squirts.
- **Hydraulic ram** [`hydraulic_ram`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/hydraulic_ram.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Many gardens on canals with a small fall would use it; valves and a pressure vessel can be made in copper.
- **Charcoal burning** [`charcoal_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/charcoal_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Wood is scarce in southern Iraq, so charcoal comes downriver or from the hills; date-palm fronds, reeds and dung fire the kilns and bath furnaces.
- **Deep coal mining (drainage, ventilation, safety lamp)** [`coal_mining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coal_mining.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. No coal near Baghdad; bitumen and naphtha seep from the ground at Hit and Kirkuk instead and serve as fuel. Local: bitumen springs at Hit; Baba Gurgur burning gas near Kirkuk.
- **Coal gas lighting** [`gas_lighting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gas_lighting.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept medium. The eternal fires of Baba Gurgur near Kirkuk burn natural gas, as do Zoroastrian fire sites near Baku. Piping it is unheard of here. Elsewhere: Sichuan: natural gas piped in bamboo to boil brine.
- **Argand lamp (hollow wick and glass chimney)** [`argand_lamp`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/argand_lamp.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Oil lamps of clay, glass and brass burn smokily; glassmakers could blow a chimney and metalworkers a hollow wick holder. Mosque lamp contractors would buy it. Local: lamp makers and mosque lamp suppliers.
- **Drilling for brine, gas and oil** [`oil_drilling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oil_drilling.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept high. Naphtha and bitumen are collected from seeps and hand-dug pits (Hit, Kirkuk, Baku) and taxed by the state. Percussion drilling is known only in Sichuan. Local: bitumen and naphtha of Hit. Elsewhere: Baku: naphtha pits; Sichuan: percussion-drilled brine wells.
- **Steam reaction toy (aeolipile)** [`steam_aeolipile`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/steam_aeolipile.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Hero's Pneumatica is known by reputation and will be studied by the Banu Musa. A sealed copper ball that spins on its own steam is a coppersmith's afternoon.
- **Boilers and the safety valve** [`safety_valve_boiler`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/safety_valve_boiler.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Bath-house boilers are open copper vats. A sealed vessel with a weighted valve is within a coppersmith's skill. Local: coppersmiths of the Suq al-Suffarin; bath-house furnaces (hammams).
- **Pistonless steam pump (Savery)** [`savery_steam_pump`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/savery_steam_pump.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Copper vessels and valves are possible; no mines need draining here, but palace gardens on high ground would.

Snow and ice from the mountains cool the drinks of the rich (well attested for later Abbasid Baghdad); porous jars and windcatchers cool by evaporation.
